newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS FINALLY LOSES AS JAYS FALL TO MARINERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS FINALLY LOSES AS JAYS FALL TO MARINERS.

text.p: After winning his first 11 decisions with the Toronto Blue Jays, a rejuvenated Roger Clemens finally suffered his first setback of the season on Wednesday.
Jeff Fassero pitched 8 1/3 strong innings to lead the Seattle Mariners to a 5-1 victory over Toronto.
"It was a beautiful game, we had plenty of chances to stay close," said Clemens. "Bottom line is Jeff pitched great."
Fassero (6-2) allowed five hits and struck out seven, falling just two outs shy of his first American League complete game. Bobby Ayala recorded the final two outs.
"I had to concentrate a lot more because of the pitcher I was throwing against," Fassero said of Clemens. "It's by far the best I've thrown on in this league."
Mariners catcher John Marzano was impressed by Fassero's effort. "He had nasty stuff, a great splitter that was almost unhittable," Marzano said. "Whatever I called, he hit the spots."
Clemens (11-1), who is tied with Bobby Jones of the New York Mets for the major league lead in wins, had won all but one of his previous 12 starts for the Blue Jays.
Clemens was charged with four earned runs and seven hits in seven-plus innings. He walked three and struck out five.
At Detroit, Curtis Pride delivered a two-out, two-run single and the Tigers scored three times in the eighth inning to defeat the Oakland Athletics 4-2.
Pinch-hitter Jody Reed hit a sacrifice fly to tie it at 2-2 before Pride singled to right field with the bases loaded, scoring Phil Nevin and Tony Clark.

Reliever Doug Brocail (1-4) won his first game since beating the Cincinnati Reds on April 19, 1996, as a member of the Houston Astros. His nine consecutive losses was the longest active losing streak in the major leagues.

At Boston, Tom Gordon tossed a four-hitter and the Red Sox capitalised on uncharacteristically poor fielding by the Baltimore Orioles to score five times in the third inning on their way to a 10-1 rout.
Gordon (4-6), who carried a two-hit shutout into the ninth, struck out seven and walked one in his second complete game of the season and 18th of his career.
He retired the first 10 batters before Roberto Alomar's single with one out in the fourth. Alomar added a double in the ninth and scored to break up the shutout.
Reggie Jefferson had four hits, two RBI and two runs scored for the Red Sox.

At Kansas City, Jose Rosado allowed one run over eight innings to win his third straight start and Chili Davis homered and drove in three runs as the Royals posted a 6-1 victory over the Anaheim Angels.
Rosado (6-3) yielded seven hits and two walks with five strikeouts. Jeff Montgomery worked the ninth for Kansas City, which has won four of its last six games.

At New York, Cecil Fielder hit a two-run homer during a four-run sixth inning and Joe Girardi had an RBI single in the eighth to snap a tie as the Yankees overcame a five-run deficit for a 7-5 victory over the Chicago White Sox.
Mark Whiten's RBI double in the eighth tied the game at 5-5 and, with the bases loaded, Girardi lined a 1-1 pitch past first baseman Dave Martinez to put the Yankees in front for good.

At Cleveland, Omar Vizquel laid down a perfect squeeze bunt and Pat Borders charged home with the winning run in the bottom of the 11th inning, giving the Indians a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers.

Sandy Alomar doubled off reliever Doug Jones (3-3) and was replaced by pinch-runner Borders. A successful Tony Fernandez bunt put the runners at the corners before Vizquel bunted the ball halfway between home plate and the mound and Borders beat the throw to the plate.
Paul Assenmacher (2-0) retired one batter in the 11th to post the win.
At Minnesota, Juan Gonzalez homered twice, doubled and drove in three runs to power the Texas Rangers to a 9-6 victory over the Twins that snapped a four-game losing streak.
Benji Gil added three hits and two RBI and Will Clark went 3-for-5 with two runs scored for Texas, which tied a season high with 18 hits against five Twins pitchers.
Gonzalez led off the fourth inning with his 11th homer of the season and smacked a two-run shot off starter Scott Aldred to highlight a five-run fifth that put Texas ahead 8-2.
John Burkett (5-5) got the win despite giving up six runs.
